category_title: Third-grade African American students who rely on picture support and skip text when overwhelmed
student_description: Tommy is a confident reader who becomes overwhelmed by high word density, leading him to skip text and over-rely on picture clues. He often makes meaning-changing miscues based on illustrations but believes he is using effective reading strategies. He uniquely needs his visual strategies validated before being redirected to explicit text chunking, as well as audio playback of his reading to help him independently recognize his errors.

criteria.rationale: Tommy is often unaware that he is skipping text or making errors, so hearing his own voice is necessary to help him recognize the disconnect between his reading and the actual text.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes recording the student's reading and playing it back to him so he can independently identify and analyze his own miscues.

criteria.rationale: To maintain Tommy's confidence and focus on actual comprehension, it is crucial to differentiate between errors that disrupt meaning and those that are harmless substitutions or dialect.
criteria.check: The long-term plan explicitly prioritizes correcting meaning-changing miscues while praising high-quality miscues and ignoring dialect-based variations.
